recovery_method: Every adapter lives under adapters/<hf_name>/ in the Hugging Face dataset, of which only revision main was used; downloads were cached locally under external/hf/<hf_name>/, which is not part of the repository. Files in results_collection/ were read first, and other files, such as per-trial results, were fetched mainly where results_collection/ lacked a side, did not match the published runs, or could not settle a task id or a run; a few READMEs, config files and sample files were also fetched for context. No single file over 60 MB was downloaded. No adapter's downloads were allowed to exceed 150 MB in total. We set both limits for this recovery.

abc-bench.formats: Both sides use the same sanitized per-round JSON written by the adapter author: results_collection/result_<side>_trial<N>.json = {side, round, agent, model, (harness), source_job, merge_rule, results: [{task_id, trial_name, reward 0|1, solved bool, raw_status}], summary: {solved, total, solve_rate_pct}}. Original side is derived from Terminal-Bench results.json is_resolved (raw_status solved / unsolved / parse_error_null); Harbor side from verifier_result.rewards.reward (raw_status solved / unsolved / errored / no_reward). run = trial number N in the file name; task_id taken verbatim.
abc-bench.notes: Outputs: data/pertask/abc-bench/original.csv and harbor.csv (672 data rows each = 3 runs x 224 tasks). Downloads (all under external/hf/abc-bench/): the 7 results_collection files plus the adapter README.md and config.yaml for context; original_parity/ and harbor_parity/ trial folders were not needed and not downloaded. Task ids: identical 224-id set in all six files, no duplicates, no rewards outside {0,1}. Note: every ABC-Bench task id contains a double underscore as part of the benchmark's own naming (task_<repo>__<feature>, e.g. task_15dkatz_official_joke_api__filtered_joke_lookup); this is not a Harbor trial suffix, so no stripping was done. The Harbor trial suffix (e.g. "__Adjb7Po") sits in the separate trial_name field and was ignored. Caveat: a large share of each round is an error state counted as reward 0 per the stated policy ("verifier errors are counted as unsolved"): original raw_status parse_error_null = 60/82/76 tasks in runs 1/2/3 (Terminal-Bench is_resolved null), Harbor raw_status errored = 66/78/86 plus 1 no_reward in run 1. So 26-38 percent of tasks per round are errors rather than clean fails; a per-task analysis may want to treat these separately (raw_status is in the source JSONs but not carried into the CSVs). NOTES.md also states that Terminal-Bench round 2 had retry/timeout/ARM-x86 rerun directories folded back into the primary results.json before publication (not independent trials), while Harbor rounds had no reruns. README lists SEMs 3.50/1.38 (sample SD) whereas the snapshot JSON lists 2.48/0.98 (SEM); run lists agree. The script takes the downloaded adapter folder as input and reads results_collection/ inside it (or the folder itself).

experiments_covered: codex@0.53.0 / gpt-5.2 (the only experiment in arc_agi_2.json; metric 'Pass@2 Rate (%)', 6 runs per side)
arc_agi_2.outcome_type: binary 0/1 per ARC test pair (pass@2: solved by at least one of two attempts). With the script's optional --per-puzzle flag the unit becomes the 120 puzzles with fractional reward (fraction of the puzzle's test pairs solved; values 0, 1/2, 2/3, 1), which is the unit of the published run scores.
arc_agi_2.validation_original: mismatch at the granularity of the CSV (per test pair, n=167): CSV run means 33.53, 40.12, 34.73, 35.93, 35.33, 37.72 vs published original_runs 34.17, 38.75, 35.42, 35.42, 34.58, 37.92 (diffs -0.64, +1.37, -0.69, +0.51, +0.75, -0.20; 0/6 within 0.1). However, re-aggregating the same rows per puzzle (mean over 120 puzzles of the fraction of test pairs solved, i.e. the official ARC-AGI-2 scoring) gives 34.17, 38.75, 35.42, 35.42, 34.58, 37.92 = exact match 6/6 in file order (run i = trial i). So the per-task data reproduce the published numbers exactly; only the aggregation unit differs.
arc_agi_2.validation_harbor: mismatch. Per test pair (CSV): 37.13, 35.93, 33.53, 32.34, 36.53, 34.73 vs published harbor_runs 35.90, 38.90, 33.33, 35.42, 36.67, 34.58 (diffs +1.23, -2.97, +0.20, -3.08, -0.14, +0.15; 0/6 within 0.1). Per puzzle (re-aggregated like the original side): 35.42, 36.25, 33.33, 33.47, 36.67, 34.58 -> runs 3, 5, 6 match exactly, runs 1, 2, 4 are off by -0.48, -2.65, -1.95. The published values for runs 1, 2, 4 equal the metrics[0].pass_at_2_rate field inside the same result files (0.359, 0.389, 0.3542), but those values cannot be reproduced from the files' own reward_stats under any definition tried (per-pair, per-puzzle fraction, per-puzzle any/all, pooled pass@2 estimator, per-attempt mean). The CSV follows reward_stats, which match the 334 trial directories on HF name-for-name and 10 spot-checked per-task result.json files.
arc_agi_2.formats: Original: results_collection/result_original_trial{1..6}.json, each a JSON list of 167 entries (one per test pair, same order in all files) of the form {"attempt_1": A, "attempt_2": A}, A = {"answer": grid, "metadata": {model, provider, timestamps, choices (full prompt/response), usage, cost, "task_id": "<puzzle>", "pair_index": int, "test_id": "codex-gpt-5-2-medium"}, "correct": bool} or null; task_id = metadata.task_id + "_" + metadata.pair_index, reward = 1 if either attempt correct. Harbor: results_collection/result_harbor_trial{1..6}.json, each a Harbor job-level result.json with stats.evals["codex__gpt-5.2__tasks"].reward_stats.reward = {"0.0": [trial names], "1.0": [trial names]} (334 names per run), trial name "<puzzle>_<pair>__<7-char suffix>"; suffix after "__" stripped, two trials per task (n_attempts: 2), reward = max over the two. Output: CSV run,task_id,reward.
arc_agi_2.notes: Outputs: data/pertask/arc_agi_2/original.csv and harbor.csv (1002 rows each = 6 runs x 167 tasks, binary, no duplicate ids, identical 167-id sets on both sides and across all runs). Usage: python scripts/pertask/arc_agi_2.py <download_dir> <out_dir> [--per-puzzle]. (1) Harbor ids carried a trial suffix "__<7 chars>" which was stripped; each run has 334 trials = 167 tasks x 2 attempts because config.yaml sets n_attempts: 2 for pass@2, so the CSV reward is the max over the two attempts; the files' per-attempt 'mean' metric (0.2665, 0.2665, 0.2365, 0.2305, 0.2545, 0.2425) is not the published score. (2) Published run scores on both sides are per-puzzle means over 120 puzzles (75 puzzles have 1 test pair, 43 have 2, 2 have 3), not per-pair means; per-pair rows were chosen as primary because they are binary, finest-grained, carry the ids exactly as in the Harbor files, and the puzzle view is derivable by grouping on the prefix before the last '_' (the --per-puzzle flag does this). Validation therefore reads 'mismatch' at pair level on both sides even though the original side reproduces all six published numbers exactly at puzzle level. (3) Harbor anomaly: for runs 1, 2 and 4 the result files' metrics[0].pass_at_2_rate (0.359, 0.389, 0.3542; note runs 1-2 are rounded to 3 decimals, the rest to 4) equals the published harbor_runs value but does not follow from the same files' reward_stats under any aggregation (per-puzzle gives 35.42, 36.25, 33.47). Evidence that reward_stats is the real per-task record: the 334 directory names in each harbor_parity/result_harbor_trialN/ on HF match the reward_stats trial names exactly, job ids match, and 10 spot-checked per-task result.json files (trials 1, 2, 4) all agree with reward_stats. Also, the HF 'trial2' folder was run locally as jobs/arc-agi-2-gpt-5-2-medium-trial-3 (trials_dir in its per-task files) while trial1 and trial4 were local trial-1 and trial-4, so a local trial-2 appears to have been dropped or replaced; the published 35.90/38.90 may come from runs not uploaded. The parity PR discussion (huggingface.co/datasets/harborframework/parity-experiments/discussions/21) may explain the difference; it was not consulted. Harbor runs 1 and 2 both have exactly 89/334 correct attempts (coincidence; the files differ). (4) Original trial 4 has one null attempt (task 16b78196_0, one of its two attempts missing); it was counted as not correct. (5) Folder contents on HF (not downloaded): original_parity/ has 6 folders result_original_trial{1..6}, each with 120 per-puzzle JSON files (~7.1 MB per trial; trial1 listed), i.e. the raw submissions, not the flat files the README describes; harbor_parity/result_harbor_trialN/ has only 334 task directories and no job-level result.json/config.json/job.log (README is out of date; the job-level files exist only in results_collection/); oracle/ has 337 task directories (3 more than 334). (6) Total download 33.36 MB, including the 10 spot-checked per-task files.
arc_agi_2.paired_note: excluded (amendment 6): Harbor runs 1, 2 and 4 do not reproduce the published per-puzzle scores; the files appear to hold runs other than the published ones. Reported as a sensitivity row.

bfcl.notes: (1) Everything downloaded is cached locally under external/hf/bfcl/ with the dataset's layout; 312 files, 4.7 MB. The oracle/ folder and the trajectory folders (original_parity/*/result/, harbor_parity/) were not downloaded. (2) The results_collection original-side files are model outputs, not scores, so the original per-task outcomes were reconstructed from the small BFCL score files in original_parity/run*/score/ (failure lists + per-category totals). Harbor renamed each id to "bfcl-" + id.replace("_","-") (e.g. bfcl-live-irrelevance-103-3-0); the parser inverts that rename (verified a bijection over the 123 tasks, zero unmatched on either side) so harbor.csv carries the same BFCL ids and the two sides join directly, as the pre-registered paired analysis (memos/phase-2-preregistration.md) needs. The raw Harbor name is recoverable from the rule above. Note Harbor's trial_name truncates long task names (bfcl-live-parallel-multiple-8-7-0 appears as bfcl-live-parallel-multiple-8-7__<hash>), so the script uses task_name, not trial_name, for the id. kumo.validation_original: match. Per-run means from original.csv (212 tasks each): run1 0.839623, run2 0.834906, run3 0.863208. Published original_trials in kumo.json: [0.839622641509434, 0.8349056603773585, 0.8632075471698113]; every run matches its same-index published value exactly (also equal to the accuracy fields in results_collection/result_original_trial{1,2,3}.json).
kumo.validation_harbor: match. Per-run means from harbor.csv (212 tasks each): run1 0.844340, run2 0.839623, run3 0.839623. Published harbor_trials in kumo.json: [0.8443396226415094, 0.839622641509434, 0.839622641509434]; every run matches its same-index published value exactly (and stats.evals[...].metrics[0].mean in each job-level file).
kumo.formats: Harbor: results_collection/result_harbor_trial<N>.json = Harbor job-level result.json, stats.evals[<eval>].reward_stats.reward = {"1.0": [trial names], "0.0": [...]}, n_errors=0, exception_stats={}; trial names "<task>__<7-char suffix>" with suffix stripped; plus 42 per-trial harbor_parity/run<N>/<trial>/result.json (fields task_name, trial_name, verifier_result.rewards.reward) used to recover 6 truncated task names per run. Original: results_collection/result_original_trial<N>.json are 180-byte aggregates ({benchmark, harness, model, eval_times, trial_index, n_tasks, accuracy}); per-task data taken from original_parity/gpt-5-nano/VanillaAgent/<Domain>/<scenario>/eval_times=3.jsonl (106 files, 2 JSONL lines each = seeds 0/1, each with "trajectories": list of 3 {successful: bool, parse_error: bool, consumed_tokens, actions, observations, generated_text} plus average_correct etc.); trajectories[j] = run j+1.
kumo.notes: results_collection has the Harbor side in full but the original side only as 3 aggregate accuracy files, so per-task original data was taken from the 106 small raw upstream eval_times=3.jsonl files under original_parity/gpt-5-nano/VanillaAgent/ (1.2 MB total, max 50 KB; these are the upstream per-(domain,scenario) output files, not Harbor trajectory folders). Task ids: a KUMO task is (domain, scenario, seed); the Harbor task name "<domain lowercased>-t<truth_num>-a<action_num>-v<valid_truth_num>-s<seed>" (e.g. algorithmenv-t4-a6-v1-s0) is used as task_id on both sides, built on the original side from the file path + seed field; the id sets are asserted identical (212 = 101 baseline domains x 2 seeds with t4-a6-v1 + 5 hard domains x 2 seeds with t12-a16-v1). Harbor trial suffix "__<7 chars>" stripped. Caveat: Harbor truncates the task-name part of trial names to 32 characters, so for mineralclassificationenv, politicalmanifestoenv and virusclassificationenv (names 33-36 chars) the trailing seed digit is cut off and seeds 0/1 collide (job-level file shows 209 unique stripped names for 212 trials). These 6 trials per run were resolved by downloading harbor_parity/run<N>/<trial>/result.json (task_name field; verifier reward asserted equal to the job-level reward) and the script requires every unparsable stripped name to be resolved this way. Original run order = trajectory index within each task (eval_times 1..3); confirmed by the exact per-run match with trial_index 1..3 accuracies. mean(successful) per task equals average_correct in every record. Original side: 11 of 636 trajectories have parse_error=true (all unsuccessful); counted as reward 0, consistent with upstream accuracy. No duplicates, no missing or extra runs, all rewards in {0.0, 1.0}. The other 5 experiments in kumo.json (kumo-vanilla/gpt-5-mini, terminus-2 and codex with gpt-5-mini/nano) are not present in the HF adapters/kumo folder (only gpt-5-nano VanillaAgent original runs and 3 Harbor runs with model openai/gpt-5-nano), so no per-task data was recovered for them. 42 per-trial config.json files were also downloaded alongside result.json; the parser does not use them. oracle/ was not downloaded. Total download 1.46 MB.

Harbor files (eval codex__gpt-5-codex__labbench): ids are trial names 'figqa-NNNN__<7-char suffix>' (suffix after '__' stripped); all 181 tasks are in reward_stats, and the AgentTimeoutError trials listed in exception_stats are also in the 0.0 bucket. Original ids were renamed run_NNNN -> figqa-NNNN so both CSVs share a key.
labbench.notes: Outputs: data/pertask/labbench/original.csv and harbor.csv (543 rows each = 3 runs x 181 tasks, task ids figqa-0001..figqa-0181, no duplicates, rewards only 0/1). (1) Task-id mapping: the original side labels tasks run_NNNN and Harbor figqa-NNNN; run_NNNN was renamed to figqa-NNNN after confirming on HF that original_parity/*/run_NNNN/prompt.txt and harbor_parity/*/figqa-NNNN__*/agent/codex.txt pose the same question for NNNN = 0003, 0100, 0181, and that run numbering is identical across the three original artifact folders (same question for run_0100 in folders 155613 and 160934, run_0181 in 155613 and 160732). Harbor trial suffixes after '__' were stripped. (2) Extra Harbor run: results_collection and the README contain a 4th Harbor trial (mean 0.392, 31 timeouts, job 2026-01-02__14-54-00) that the snapshot JSON omits (snapshot lists 3 trials and its harbor mean 0.411 is the 3-trial mean; README's 0.406 is the 4-trial mean). harbor.csv contains trials 1-3 only; setting HARBOR_RUNS = (1, 2, 3, 4) in the script adds it. Harbor_parity job folders map to trials by start time: 2025-12-25__14-55-41 = trial1, 2025-12-26__11-12-24 = trial2, 2026-01-02__13-01-59 = trial3, 2026-01-02__14-54-00 = trial4. (3) High no-answer rates on both sides, all scored 0: Harbor AgentTimeoutError on 20/31/35 of 181 trials per run (11-19%); original NoAnswer+ParseError on 24/31/24 of 181 (13-17%). On the original side these errored runs are absent from reward_stats (listed only in exception_stats); scoring them 0 reproduces the published accuracy = correct/181 exactly, and the file's separate precision metric (correct/answered, 0.459/0.483/0.465) confirms the accuracy denominator is 181. One original run (trial 2, run_0095) is flagged 'unsure' and is already in the 0.0 bucket. (4) The three original_parity/codex_artifacts_*/result.json files are JSON-identical to result_original_trial1/2/3.json respectively (155613 -> trial1, 160732 -> trial2, 160934 -> trial3), so results_collection is a faithful copy. (5) Original_parity run folders contain per-run prompt.txt, answer.txt, expected_answer.txt, unsure_answer.txt, codex_trajectory.json and figure images (one 3.6 MB jpg per run), so no whole trajectory folders were downloaded; total download 124,844 bytes. The published original trial-3 score appears in the README as '0. 403' (typo); snapshot JSON has 0.403.

lawbench.formats: Harbor: results_collection/result_harbor_trial{1,2,3}.json = Harbor job-level result.json, stats.evals["qwen-coder__lawbench"].reward_stats.reward = {"<reward>": [trial names]}, n_trials=120, n_errors=0; trial names "lawbench-<scenario>-<chunk>-<prompt>__<7-char suffix>", suffix after "__" stripped. lawbench.notes: (1) results_collection/ holds only the 3 Harbor files; the original side came from original_parity/, which contains exactly 3 small summary JSONs (result_origin_trial{1,2,3}.json, ~13.4 KB each) and nothing else -- no trajectories were downloaded. harbor_parity/ (3 job dirs) and oracle/harbor-oracle/ were not downloaded. Total download 92,669 bytes, 8 files. (2) Harbor ids carried a "__<suffix>" trial suffix that was stripped; original ids were composed from the prompt key and chunk key. After that, both sides' 120 ids are identical to each other and to the 120 task_names in config.yaml, and are identical across all 3 runs per side. (3) No missing or extra runs, no duplicate (run, task) rows, no errors (n_errors=0). All rewards in [0,1]; Harbor trial 2 contains two rewards of ~1.65e-16 (floating-point zero from the LawBench scorer), kept verbatim in harbor.csv. (4) Minor: the snapshot JSON quotes +/- 0.3 (original) / 0.7 (harbor) while the adapter README quotes +/- 0.4 / 1.0 for the same three trials (different SD convention); the trial values themselves agree everywhere. Outputs: data/pertask/lawbench/original.csv and harbor.csv (360 rows each).

livecodebench.outcome_type: binary 0/1 on both sides (original: is_resolved true -> 1 else 0; harbor: reward_stats value 1.0/0.0, errored trials -> 0)
livecodebench.validation_original: match (as a multiset; file order differs from published order). Per-run means from original.csv x100: run1=56.0, run2=52.0, run3=52.0, run4=58.0 (100 tasks each). livecodebench.formats: Original side: results_collection/result_original_trail<k>.json (note 'trail', sic) is a terminal-bench job results JSON: {"id", "results": [{task_id, trial_name, is_resolved (true/false/null), failure_mode, parser_results {test name: 'passed'/...}, ...}], "pass_at_k", "n_resolved", "n_unresolved", "resolved_ids", "unresolved_ids", "accuracy"}; 100 records per file. reward = 1.0 if is_resolved is true else 0.0; is_resolved is null for 26/31/27/28 trials per run (failure_mode test_timeout or parse_error) and those count as unresolved, exactly as the file's accuracy = n_resolved/100 and unresolved_ids do (cross-checked: resolved_ids == {is_resolved true}; is_resolved == all parser_results 'passed' with zero mismatches). task_id = 'task_id' field verbatim, no suffix. Harbor side: results_collection/result_harbor_trial<k>.json is the Harbor job-level result: stats.evals['claude-code__claude-haiku-4-5__release_v6'].reward_stats.reward = {'1.0': [...], '0.0': [...]} plus exception_stats = {'VerifierTimeoutError': [...], 'AgentTimeoutError': [...]}; n_total_trials 100. Trial names carry a '__<7-char>' suffix (e.g. 'abc333_a__d3XHriC'), stripped to the LiveCodeBench question id. Trials only in exception_stats (24/28/27/29 per run) get reward 0.0. Task ids are LiveCodeBench question ids like 'abc333_a', 'arc195_c', '1873_d', '3608' and are identical across all 8 files.
livecodebench.notes: (1) Only one of the two snapshot experiments is recoverable: the 'original' side on HF is the terminal-bench adapter run (TB -> Harbor parity with claude-code / claude-haiku-4-5), not the upstream LiveCodeBench harness; the gpt-5-mini/terminus-2 experiment (Original LCB vs TB) has no files in the dataset. (2) Original file names are spelled result_original_trail<k>.json ('trail'); the parser accepts both spellings. (3) Original run numbering: file trail1..4 correspond to published tb_adapter_trials in a different order (file means 56,52,52,58 vs published 58,52,52,56); Harbor file order matches published order. (4) Error rates are high on both sides: original has 26-31 null is_resolved per run (22-25 test_timeout + 2-6 parse_error) and Harbor has 24-29 exception trials per run (22-25 VerifierTimeoutError + 2-4 AgentTimeoutError); all are scored 0, consistent with each file's own accuracy/mean and with the published numbers. (5) Harbor runs 2, 3, 4 list one or two trials under both reward '0.0' and exception AgentTimeoutError (run2 arc195_c, run3 arc195_c, run4 abc301_f and arc195_c); the reward value (0.0) is used, so there is no effect, and each run has exactly 100 unique task ids after stripping the '__<suffix>' trial id. (6) Task id sets are identical across all 8 files (100 ids, 100 common). (7) Rewards are strictly in {0.0, 1.0}: original 218 ones / 182 zeros, harbor 213 ones / 187 zeros over 400 rows each. (8) The adapter README.md (4680 B) and config.yaml (480 B) were also downloaded for context but not parsed. README says verifier timeout 180 s while config.yaml says override_timeout_sec 60.0. (9) No trial folders were downloaded from original_parity/ or harbor_parity/ (4 dated folders each); results_collection sufficed.
livecodebench.paired_note: The 'original' side of these files is the Terminal-Bench adapter run (transitive leg), so the adapter is reported in the secondary set, not the headline paired set.

llmsr_bench.formats: Both sides use the same custom JSON summary (not the Harbor job-level stats.evals layout), one file per run: results_collection/result_<harbor|original>_trial<k>.json = {"trials": [{"trial": k, "seed": k-1, "tasks": [{"dataset": one of bio_pop_growth/chem_react/lsrtransform/matsci/phys_osc, "problem": benchmark id (e.g. BPG0, CRK3, I.11.19_2_0, MatSci7, PO12), "metrics": {r2, mse, nmse, ood_r2, ood_mse, ood_nmse}}]}]}. The published failure filter (r2 <= -100 or nmse >= 1e9) is applied but drops nothing.
llmsr_bench.notes: (1) Outputs: data/pertask/llmsr_bench/original.csv and harbor.csv, 345 rows each (3 runs x 115 tasks, 23 tasks per dataset). Task id sets and even task order are identical across all six files; no duplicates; no missing or extra runs. (2) The snapshot disagrees with the published files: the local llmsr_bench.json run lists (original [0.7712,0.7630,0.7950], harbor [0.7543,0.7613,0.7811]; headline 0.7764±0.0096 vs 0.7656±0.0080) do not match the per-task files, while the HF README in the same folder (headline Original 0.776162±0.0105, Harbor 0.790201±0.00207, per-trial means listed) matches the CSV means to 4 decimals on both sides. The snapshot values are not a permutation of the file values and the Harbor headline differs by ~2.5 points, so the snapshot JSON appears to predate a re-run/update of the published results (snapshot date 2026-02-26; harbor_jobs dirs are also timestamped 2026-02-26). The parity-PR discussion (#207) or an older HF revision of results_collection may hold the files the snapshot was built from; only revision main was fetched, so this was not checked. The pinned snapshot values are kept as published, and the adapter is excluded from the per-task analyses (validation_ok is false on both sides). (3) Rewards are unclipped R2 and 15 rows per side are negative (see outcome_type); clipping to 0 would move run means by up to ~0.44 pts (original run 3), so they were left as published. (4) Not downloaded, for reference: harbor_parity/harbor_jobs holds 345 timestamped per-task job dirs (= 115 x 3); origin_parity holds 5 dataset dirs (LSR_Transform, bio_pop_growth, chem_react, matsci, phys_osc) each with an LlmDirect-GPT4o-mini/ subdir of raw original-repo outputs; oracle holds 240 task dirs plus config.json (1.9 KB), job.log (0 B), result.json (17.6 KB). (5) The README also mentions a codex + gpt-4o-mini Harbor-only baseline (R2 0.511961); no per-task file for it exists in results_collection and it is not in the snapshot JSON. (6) Harbor task directory names are a lossy lowercase rendering of the file ids ("llmsr-bench-<dataset>-<problem lowercased, dots to dashes>__<suffix>"); task_id keeps the files' own "<dataset>/<problem>" form instead.

medagentbench.notes: Outputs: data/pertask/medagentbench/{original,harbor}.csv, 900 rows each (3 runs x 300 tasks), no duplicate (run, task_id), all rewards in {0,1}, identical task-id sets on both sides (task1_1..task10_30, 10 categories x 30 instances). Harbor trial suffixes after "__" were stripped. Original-side task ids are positional: the official overall.json entries have only "index" 0..299 (no id field), so task_id = task{index//30+1}_{index%30+1}, assuming the official test_data_v2.json order task1_1..task1_30, task2_1, ..., task10_30. This was verified three ways before use: (1) each block of 30 indices holds exactly one question template and the ten templates are MedAgentBench categories 1..10 in order (MRN lookup, age, record BP, recent Mg, Mg order, avg CBG, recent CBG, ortho referral, K order, HbA1C); the question at each index is identical across the three original trials; (2) per-category success rates agree closely across sides; (3) per-task agreement between original and Harbor runs under this mapping is 0.97-0.99, the same as run-to-run agreement within either side (0.97-0.99), versus ~0.83 (max 0.87 over 200 draws) for a random within-category shuffle; e.g. category 4 fails on exactly the same 11 instances in all six runs. Residual caveat: within-block ordering is inferred, not read from an id field. Extra run: results_collection/ also holds result_harbor_terminus2_trial1.json (Terminus-2 + gpt-4o-mini, 1 run, 49.00%, same 300 task ids, same Harbor format). It is a different agent, is not in the snapshot JSON's run lists, and was deliberately skipped (noted in the script docstring). Categories 7, 9, 10 score 0 in every run on both sides (ceiling/floor effects for paired analysis); categories 1 and 3 score 1.0 everywhere. Downloads (17.9 MB total): results_collection/ (7 files), README.md, config.yaml, parity_experiment.json, and the two tiny READMEs in original_parity/ and harbor_parity/. Not downloaded, for reference: original_parity/ contains the same three ~5.9 MB result_original_trial{1,2,3}.json files plus README.md (289 B); harbor_parity/ contains README.md (364 B) and four job directories (medagentbench-parity-agent-full300, -trial2, -trial3, and medagentbench-terminus2-gpt4omini-full300-v3-c12-mt8), each said to hold result.json and config.json. Harbor: results_collection/harbor-trial{1,2,3}.json = Harbor job-level result.json, stats.evals["terminus-2__gpt-4o__mmau"].reward_stats.reward = {"0.0": [...], "1.0": [...]} plus exception_stats; trial names are "<first 32 chars of the uuid>__<7-char suffix>". task_id on both sides = the full 36-char MMAU uuid exactly as in the original files.
mmau.notes: Outputs: data/pertask/mmau/original.csv and harbor.csv (3000 rows each, no duplicate (run,task_id), rewards all in {0,1}, identical 1000-task set across runs and sides). (1) Main caveat: the two sides are per-task identical. For each run k, original run k and Harbor run k agree on every task (1000/1000 in runs 1 and 3; 999/1000 in run 2, the sole disagreement being the errored Harbor trial, which scores 1 on the original side). Runs within a side differ on 114-125 tasks, so this is not chance determinism: the two sides evidently share the same model outputs (one side's outcomes are effectively a re-scoring/copy of the other's). For paired statistics the sides are not independent samples, and the entire original-vs-harbor difference is the single errored trial. (2) Original side has no correctness field; rewards were recomputed with MMAU's string_match rule re-implemented from the benchmark's evaluation.py. It reproduces the published run scores exactly; exact string match does not (578/549/560). (3) Harbor trial names are 32-char truncations of the 36-char MMAU uuid plus a "__<7-char>" suffix; the suffix was stripped and the prefix mapped back to the full uuid via the original-side id list (mapping unique, no collisions, all 2999 trials mapped), so both CSVs use the full uuid as task_id. (4) Harbor run 2: 999 scored trials + 1 RewardFileNotFoundError (c65b8ad2-2c5e-46f1-9041-1df1595003de), written as reward 0.0 following the repo convention (reproduces metrics mean 0.552 and published 55.20). (5) Two different copies of original trial 2 exist on HF: original_parity/original-parity-trial2.json (816,981 B) has the same records in the same order as results_collection/original-trial2.json (816,787 B) but model_output differs on 181 tasks and it scores 561/1000; the snapshot JSON (55.30) matches the results_collection copy, which is what the CSV uses. The README's tables (Original = Harbor = 0.581/0.561/0.564) reflect the original_parity copy for trial 2 and disagree with the snapshot on both sides; original_parity trials 1 and 3 have byte-identical sizes to their results_collection copies (not downloaded). (6) results_collection also holds gpt-4o-trial{1,2,3}.json, a "gpt-4o without agent" experiment (string_match 569/568/573, matching the README) that is not in mmau.json; ignored. (7) Other HF folders (not downloaded): original_parity/ = 3 JSON files ~817 KB each; harbor_parity/ = 3 job dirs (mmau-gpt4o-trial{1,2,3}) each with 1000 trial subdirs and no job-level result.json at the top; gpt-4o/ = 3 JSON files with the same sizes as the results_collection copies; oracle/ = 1000 trial dirs. 12 files downloaded, 5,946,372 bytes.
